## Highlights

- Deployment verification with `tale deploy accept` now accepts third-party Docker images whose
  optional labels are absent, and valid Docker timestamps with timezone offsets. Tale images
  still require the expected source and version, and verification still refuses a container
  that changes while it is being checked.
  [#4512](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4512)
- Concurrent sandbox watchdog passes now finish recording the sessions they inspected
  without deadlocking with each other. The update locks overlapping session records in a
  consistent order; the individual checks still run concurrently.
  [#4518](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4518)
- Automation runs record when another worker takes over and show **Interrupted — resuming**
  or **Resumed after a restart**. Completed steps keep their results. If an interrupted
  connector write may already have reached its service, the run can wait for a decision:
  check the service, then choose **Run it again**, **Skip it** or **Fail the run** on the run
  page. No notification is sent for this wait. Concurrent runs also keep their approval
  checks separate, and approving a waiting step wakes its run immediately.
  A decision about an earlier attempt is refused after that step has retried, so an old
  confirmation cannot resolve a newer interrupted write.
  [#4516](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4516),
  [#4528](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4528)
- The automation editor checks a draft as you edit and groups its problems by step. Selecting
  a problem opens the affected field; Save and Deploy explain which errors must be fixed.
  Checks handle quoted template delimiters correctly and bound complex code analysis to keep
  the editor responsive; see the new limits in the upgrade notes below.
  [#4521](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4521),
  [#4534](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4534)
- New project task runs with the agent's full permissions can recover from a brief connection
  or service failure during an eligible GET request for a brokered credential. The bounded
  retry checks that the task is still allowed to start. Member-confined runs, POST brokers
  and account cooldowns keep their existing behavior; see
  [Task automation](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/projects/task-automation).
  Codex model-capacity failures use a counted automatic retry with a one-minute minimum delay,
  keeping the account eligible and the conversation available, including after checkpoint
  recovery. They do not trigger an immediate fresh conversation on a resumed turn. Existing
  retry and hourly start limits still apply; workflow agent steps keep their existing capacity
  handling.
  [#4523](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4523),
  [#4529](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4529)
- The navigation rail and phone tabs now open each section's overview instead of the last
  page visited. On a computer, **Home** opens a new chat and **Settings** opens **Account** for
  every role; **Knowledge** opens **Documents**, and **Automations** opens its list. Automations
  opened from a project keep that project in their breadcrumbs and highlight **Automations**
  in the rail.
  [#4514](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4514)
- Excel imports check required columns against the worksheet's header row. Blank cells in the
  first data row no longer make a present column look missing and reject the whole file;
  imported rows keep their spreadsheet row numbers.
  [#4390](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4390)
- CSV import results keep the original source row numbers, including when blank rows are
  skipped, so a reported problem points back to the correct row.
  [#4201](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4201)
- A failed document-folder breadcrumb request now shows its error and can recover on a later
  successful request. A missing or inaccessible folder returns to Documents with an explanation.
  [#4326](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4326)
- Opening a conversation in the **Inbox** now marks it read whenever it has unread messages.
  Before, a message that arrived late with an earlier timestamp, such as a delayed or backfilled
  one, could leave the conversation unread after it was opened.
  [#4397](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4397)
- A product save that finishes after the **Add product** dialog was closed and reopened from
  outside, or after the organization changed, no longer closes the dialog or clears the newer
  draft.
  [#4417](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4417)
- In **Add contact** and **Edit contact**, invalid phone characters stay visible with an inline
  error, and **Save** is blocked until they are removed. A value such as `+41abc` is no longer
  silently saved as `+41`; valid number formatting is preserved.
  [#4402](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4402)
- In French, the audit log's legal hold entries, such as requested, approved and refused releases,
  and the messages that refuse to delete a project or the organization under a hold now say
  **conservation légale**, as Governance does. The French guides use **conservation** for an
  individual legal hold, replacing the remaining "gel" wording.
  [#4502](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4502),
  [#4510](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4510)
- The German and French guides call connectors **Connector** and **Connectors**, the name the app
  shows, instead of "Connectoren", "Konnektoren" or "connecteurs". The documented path to OAuth
  apps matches the app: **Einstellungen > Connectors > OAuth-Apps** in German and
  **Paramètres > Connectors > Apps OAuth** in French. Links to the renamed headings keep working.
  [#4500](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4500)

## Upgrade notes

- Back up the application and knowledge databases, configuration, keys and external stores
  before deploying. Application migrations `0160`–`0163` add automation run leases, recovery
  history, a record of calls made by each step and the protocol-2 writer fence. The release
  candidate source contract (`.github/release-candidate-contract.json`) is unchanged.
- Deploy this release's CLI and matching Tale runtime images together through the normal full
  deployment path, then verify the new deployment. A configuration-only update does not install
  these fixes. If a v0.5.77 deployment reached Ready but failed acceptance on Docker metadata, its
  earlier failed verification remains failed; use the new deployment's acceptance result.
- The first upgrade from v0.5.77 holds older queued, running and waiting automation runs.
  They show **On hold** with their earlier progress and unknown external outcomes; they do
  not resume automatically. Already-admitted work or an external operation may still finish.
  Check the external service before taking further action. **Request stop** records your
  acknowledgement and requests cancellation of the owned session; it does not prove termination,
  undo an external effect or release the hold. The run, its evidence and its task remain protected
  from deletion or replacement while held.
  [#4539](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4539)
- After the protocol cutover, use a compatible runtime and this release's CLI to repair forward.
  The CLI checks the installed database floor and the immutable backend image before deployment
  or rollback, and refuses an older or unverifiable target. A protocol-2 backend already created
  for a pending deployment also requires a compatible target. Older CLIs and manual Docker
  commands do not implement this guard; a snapshot cannot undo external effects or authorize
  an older runtime against the migrated database. The tag-based guard currently supports only
  the bundled application database: an explicit `DATABASE_URL`, custom `APP_DB_NAME` or installed
  backend pointing elsewhere is refused. It does not start a stopped database to inspect it.
  Keep the existing runtime and repair the readback; removing an override or using an older CLI
  does not establish compatibility. See
  [Upgrades](https://docs.tale.dev/self-hosted/operate/upgrades).
- For your own Compose setup, allow at least the shipped stop grace: `backend-api` gets
  `30s` and `backend-worker` gets `120s`. The new optional `SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_MS` defaults to
  `15000` for the API and `90000` for a worker; keep stop grace at least 15 seconds above a
  longer drain setting. The matching CLI generates these values. The optional
  `AUTOMATION_ORG_CONCURRENCY` defaults to `8` automation steps per organization across
  workers; `0` disables that limit. Keep clocks synchronized across worker hosts.
- REST/OpenAPI contract `3.20.0` includes run resumption fields, `waitingFor: in_doubt`, the
  `engine_incompatible` and `effect_in_doubt` failure codes, and the held-run status and public
  hold details. It also adds an explicit held-run stop request with acknowledgement and stale-state
  checks. Update clients that exhaustively handle run states and error codes. An uncertain
  individual write is still decided in the app; its decision is separate from a legacy run's
  stop request.
- MCP automation authoring responses also include the contract `3.19.0` additions:
  `validate_automation` returns `analysis` and `types`, with issue locations in `at`, `params`
  and `related`; `save_automation` returns warnings, and `get_catalog` includes each capability's
  `outputSchema`. Revalidate custom automations: references are parsed, agent `files` contribute
  dependencies, and `ITEM_WITHOUT_FOREACH` is now an error. Recognized static-analysis warnings
  remain advisory during configuration deployment; missing resources and unrecognized warnings
  still stop deployment.
- Each automation expression and `transform` body now has analysis limits of 8192 UTF-16 code
  units, 512 JavaScript tokens and 64 levels of syntax or syntax-tree nesting. Whitespace around
  a template expression and plain text outside templates do not count toward its size; whitespace
  in a `transform` body does. Previously valid code can exceed these limits: shorten it or split
  the work across nodes before saving or deploying again. See
  [Automation concepts](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/automations/concepts).
- When upgrading from v0.5.76 or earlier, also apply the
  [v0.5.77 upgrade notes](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/releases/tag/v0.5.77) and the
  earlier requirements they link. They include a full deployment for the Bun 1.4.2 runtime, a
  proxy that passes the `Tale-Serving-Identity` header for `tale deploy accept`, a review of the
  contract digest if you pin it, and granting `task_delegate_review` only after deploying.
- Known issues carried into this release:
  - The built-in **Triage GitHub issues** and **Review GitHub pull requests** schedules lack the
    required repository inputs (`owner` and `repo`). Static analysis reports
    `TRIGGER_INPUT_MISMATCH`; the new editor checks do not repair those schedules.
  - When a reply uses a tool, such as a document search, before it answers, **Message
    information** counts the tool's time as model time: the bar draws it as waiting for the model
    or thinking, and **Output speed** can include it.
    [#4493](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4493)
  - The projects overview still describes the **Environment** editor's earlier name check and the
    tab's earlier wording about task runtimes. Where they differ, the tab and its editor are
    current.
    [#4454](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4454)
  - Some page titles and text on the German website still say Agents and Governance instead of
    **Agenten** and **Richtlinien**.
    [#4483](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4483)
